summary: Picks which ripgrep binary find's per-term scans run: COLDSTART_RG env (always wins) → `rg` on PATH → bundled @vscode/ripgrep → editor-app copies (VS Code/Cursor; the Claude Code binary is ripgrep when run with argv0=rg); each candidate must answer `--version` with 'ripgrep'. The winner is persisted machine-wide in ~/.coldstart/searcher.json (e.g. {"bin":"rg"}) and later runs trust it without re-probing; a scan-time spawn failure calls invalidateRg() to re-resolve once. No ripgrep → find.ts falls back to git grep → grep → Node scan. It only chooses the binary: find being slow on a big repo is NOT a searcher-resolution problem when searcher.json says rg (see find.ts collectCoverage).
